name: Code and abstract inpatient, day surgery and emergency charts for CIHI
summary: After every inpatient stay, day surgery and emergency visit, health records staff assemble the chart and coders turn it into a standard abstract: diagnoses in ICD-10-CA, procedures in CCI and administrative fields, which the hospital submits to CIHI's Discharge Abstract Database and National Ambulatory Care Reporting System. The data drives provincial funding, wait-time reporting and research. Coding is slowed by charts that arrive without a discharge summary, physicians who answer queries late, and monthly deadlines that push coders to meet quotas with unspecified codes.

baseline.org_archetype: A three-site Ontario community hospital corporation with a hybrid electronic and scanned paper chart, about 30 coders and a commercial coding and abstracting tool with CIHI edits.
baseline.notes: Emergency visits are coded from the electronic ED record; inpatient and day surgery charts still contain scanned paper.

unit_of_work: one chart abstract (inpatient stay, day surgery visit or ED visit)
trigger: The patient is discharged in the ADT system and an abstract shell appears on the coding worklist.
end_state: The coded abstract has passed edits and been accepted in the hospital's DAD or NACRS submission to CIHI.

volume.seasonality: ED volumes peak in winter; elective day surgery fell sharply in spring 2020 and during later COVID-19 pauses, then rose during recovery.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate kept; it agrees with about 13,000 ED visits, 2,300 inpatient discharges plus newborns and 3,000 to 3,800 day surgery and endoscopy visits a month.

surge.cause: fiscal year-end (March to May) and month-end backlog clearance

evidence.note: Ontario's year-end DAD and NACRS deadline is earlier than other provinces' (cihi_deadlines); the size of the push is the author's estimate.

Coders abstract inpatient and ambulatory charts against a daily quota (lucyk2017). FTE is the author's estimate from hands-on time and volume; the organisation file lists 30 coders, some of whom do reabstraction, data quality and release-of-information backup. Loaded costs are the organisation file's ranges: hourly wage x 1.35 (about 25% benefits and HOOPP pension plus 10% overhead). Physician costs are gross clinical earnings paid by the province, not hospital payroll. Roles added here use the same 1.35 factor.

roles.title: Health records clerk (release of information, scanning)

evidence.note: Records staff assemble charts and pass them to coders (lucyk2017). FTE is the author's estimate.
Health information managers monitor quotas and month-end submission timelines (lucyk2017). FTE is the author's estimate.
Physicians complete discharge summaries, often late (oag2010, lucyk2017), and answer coder queries. Stands for all attending physicians; author's FTE estimate.
Completes missing operative reports for day surgery charts. Author's estimate.
Completes missing ED physician records and time stamps. Author's estimate.

systems.name: Coding and abstracting software with CIHI DAD and NACRS edits
Hospital information system (electronic patient record with ADT, order entry, results, eMAR and clinical documentation)
Document imaging and scanning of paper chart forms
Email, telephone, pagers and wireless phones

steps.name: Create the abstract on the coding worklist
steps.description: When the patient is discharged in the ADT system, an interface creates an abstract in the coding software with demographics, health card number, admission and discharge dates and service, and places it on the worklist for its type: inpatient, day surgery or emergency.

evidence.note: Mix is the author's estimate from the organisation file's drivers: about 13,000 ED visits, 2,300 inpatient discharges plus newborns, and 3,000 to 3,800 day surgery and endoscopy visits a month.

steps.name: Prepare and scan the inpatient chart
steps.description: A health records clerk collects the paper chart from the unit, removes staples, sorts the documents into the standard order, adds barcoded cover sheets and scans them into document imaging, then checks image quality.

error.defect_description: Pages scanned to the wrong encounter or out of order

evidence.note: Charts move to health records to be organised and assembled; poorly ordered multi-volume charts can consume half a coder's time (lucyk2017). Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the chart for missing documents
steps.description: The clerk runs deficiency analysis: checks for the discharge summary, operative notes, consultation reports and signatures, and assigns each missing item to the responsible physician's electronic in-box.

next.condition: chart complete (45%), or coded from available documents to meet month-end (20%)
waits for the physician to complete it

evidence.note: A coder estimated up to 80% of charts reached coding without a discharge summary, and coders coded from available documents to meet quotas (lucyk2017, Alberta). Ontario shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete the deficient documents
steps.description: The physician opens the deficiency in-box, dictates or signs the discharge summary or other missing reports, and authenticates transcribed documents so the chart can be coded.

control.basis: Medical staff rules and by-laws on health record completion, with suspension of admitting privileges for overdue records

evidence.note: At three Ontario hospitals, 90%, 72% and 7% of discharge summaries were signed within 10 days; 90% took up to 32 or 139 days at two of them (oag2010).

steps.name: Chase overdue records
steps.description: The clerk sends overdue-record notices, adds the physician to the incomplete-records list reported to the chief of staff, and warns of suspension of admitting privileges under the medical staff rules.

evidence.note: One hospital suspended admitting privileges for summaries not completed within 10 working days (oag2010). Notice cycle is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Code the inpatient stay
steps.description: The coder reads the discharge summary, progress notes, consultations, operative and diagnostic reports, selects the most responsible diagnosis and comorbidities with their diagnosis types in ICD-10-CA, and codes interventions in CCI.

error.defect_description: Unspecified or wrong most responsible diagnosis, changing the case mix group and weight

evidence.note: Coders abstract up to 30 inpatient charts a day, about 25 on average, using many document types (lucyk2017); all DAD records use ICD-10-CA and CCI (cihi_dad_meta).

steps.name: Query the physician
steps.description: The coder writes a query in the physician's in-box or on a query form asking for clarification, for example whether documented urinary infection with sepsis criteria is sepsis, without leading the physician to an answer.

evidence.note: CIHI standards say coders should return charts to physicians for clarification, but the practice was discouraged at urban Alberta sites (lucyk2017). Share and minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Answer the coder query
steps.description: The physician reads the query, reviews the chart and writes an addendum clarifying the diagnosis, or does not answer before the month-end deadline, in which case the coder uses the less specific code.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete the abstract and run edits
steps.description: The coder enters the remaining abstract fields (admission category, special care unit days, ALC days, intervention attributes), runs the coding software edits and the grouper to see the case mix group and weight, and fixes edit errors.

error.defect_description: ALC days or special care days entered incorrectly

control.basis: CIHI DAD and NACRS submission requirements mandated by the Ontario Ministry of Health (hospital service accountability agreement reporting)

evidence.note: DAD abstracts are submitted electronically and validated by CIHI (cihi_dad_meta). Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the day surgery record
steps.description: The clerk collects the day surgery or endoscopy record, checks that the operative or procedure report and anaesthetic record are present, and scans the paper parts into document imaging.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Code and abstract the day surgery visit
steps.description: The coder codes the main problem and procedures from the operative report, enters the anaesthetic and visit fields for the ambulatory abstract, runs edits and saves it as complete.

error.defect_description: Intervention attribute or approach coded wrongly

control.basis: CIHI DAD and NACRS submission requirements mandated by the Ontario Ministry of Health (hospital service accountability agreement reporting)

evidence.note: Ambulatory and emergency coders abstract up to 180 charts a day (lucyk2017); day surgery takes longer than ED. Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Dictate the missing operative report
steps.description: The surgeon receives the deficiency notice and dictates or signs the operative report so the procedure can be coded from the surgeon's own description.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Code and abstract the emergency visit
steps.description: The coder opens the electronic ED record and triage note, codes the main problem and any interventions, and checks the ED-specific fields that feed provincial wait-time reports: triage level and time, physician initial assessment time, decision to admit and departure times, and disposition.

error.defect_description: Wrong main problem or missing time stamp affecting ED wait-time reports

control.basis: CIHI DAD and NACRS submission requirements mandated by the Ontario Ministry of Health (hospital service accountability agreement reporting)

next.condition: physician record or time stamp missing

evidence.note: Up to 180 ambulatory and emergency charts a day (lucyk2017). Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase the missing ED documentation
steps.description: The clerk sends the ED physician a deficiency for the unsigned or missing ED record, or asks the ED unit clerk to correct a missing time stamp in the tracking board record.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete the ED physician record
steps.description: The emergency physician opens the deficiency on the next shift, completes or signs the ED record, and adds the final diagnosis, disposition and any missing times.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review a sample of abstracts for quality
steps.description: A senior coder re-codes a sample of abstracts, compares diagnoses, diagnosis types and interventions with the original, corrects errors and gives feedback to the coder.

evidence.note: Coders reported little feedback from management on coding quality (lucyk2017). Sample size and minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run month-end completeness and data quality checks
steps.description: At month-end the health information manager reconciles abstracts against ADT discharges, chases uncoded charts, runs data quality reports and assigns casual coders to backlogs to meet the submission date. Minutes are the per-abstract share.

evidence.note: In Alberta all abstracts for a month are due on the 21st of the next month, and casual coders work toward month-end to meet quotas (lucyk2017). Ontario's monthly cycle is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Submit the abstracts to CIHI
steps.description: The coding software builds the DAD and NACRS submission files, the manager uploads them through CIHI's electronic data submission service, and CIHI returns an error and correction report.

control.basis: CIHI DAD and NACRS submission requirements mandated by the Ontario Ministry of Health (hospital service accountability agreement reporting)

evidence.note: Facilities submit electronic files; CIHI tests integrity and validates, and asks for quarterly submissions within 60 days of quarter end, with an earlier year-end deadline for Ontario (cihi_dad_meta, cihi_deadlines; current pages). Error share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Correct rejected abstracts
steps.description: The coder opens each abstract listed on the CIHI error report, fixes the invalid code or field combination, and the corrected record goes in the next submission.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Chart coded without a discharge summary
exceptions.description: To meet month-end, the coder codes an inpatient stay from progress notes and admission diagnoses; the diagnoses may differ from those at discharge and are rarely revisited.

exceptions.name: Overdue physician records
exceptions.description: The physician does not complete the discharge summary after reminders, the chart is listed for suspension and coding waits weeks.

exceptions.name: CIHI rejection
exceptions.description: An abstract fails CIHI validation and is corrected and resubmitted in a later file.

benchmarks.unit: days from discharge to accepted submission
benchmarks.population: all abstracts in an Ontario community hospital

evidence.note: Author's estimate based on a monthly submission cycle: in Alberta each month's abstracts are due on the 21st of the next month, i.e. 21 to 51 days after discharge (lucyk2017); CIHI asks for quarterly submissions within 60 days of quarter end (cihi_dad_meta).

benchmarks.unit: inpatient charts per coder per day (average; up to 30)

evidence.note: Interview-based study of 28 coders; up to 180 ambulatory and emergency charts a day.

pain_points.description: Charts reach coders without discharge summaries, so coders wait or code from incomplete documents.

evidence.note: Up to 80% of charts estimated incomplete at one Alberta site (lucyk2017); Ontario summary completion within 10 days ranged 7% to 90% (oag2010).

pain_points.description: Quotas and monthly deadlines push coders toward unspecified codes and discourage physician queries.

evidence.note: Coders reported quantity over quality and that returning charts to physicians was discouraged.

pain_points.description: Disorganised scanned or paper charts slow coding.

evidence.note: A three-volume unorganised chart can take half the coding time.

sources.title: Barriers to data quality resulting from the process of coding health information to administrative data: a qualitative study (Lucyk, Tang and Quan)
sources.supports: Coding workflow, documentation sources, incomplete charts, physician query practice, daily quotas (25 average, up to 30 inpatient, up to 180 ambulatory/ED), monthly submission deadline in Alberta, month-end casual coders.

sources.title: 2010 Annual Report, Chapter 3, Section 3.02: Discharge of Hospital Patients
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Discharge summary completion times at three Ontario hospitals and suspension of admitting privileges for overdue summaries.

sources.title: Discharge Abstract Database (DAD) metadata
sources.supports: DAD coded in ICD-10-CA and CCI; electronic submission and validation; quarterly submission targets within 60 days.

sources.title: Submission deadlines and refresh dates
sources.supports: DAD and NACRS submission deadlines, including the earlier Ontario-only year-end deadline.

assumptions: One case is one abstract. Emergency visits make up about two-thirds of the volume but little of the effort; inpatient stays take most coder time.
The hospital submits DAD and NACRS monthly, so coded abstracts wait for the month-end cycle; the batch wait is the main part of the elapsed time.
The simulated median (about 21 days) sits below the 28-day benchmark because two-thirds of abstracts are ED visits coded within days; inpatient abstracts alone run closer to 30 days.
Physician steps use hospitalist for all attending physicians, surgeon for operative reports and ed_physician for ED records.
Coder FTE (26) is below the organisation file's 30 coder headcount; the gap is assumed to cover reabstraction, data requests, vacancies and leave.
The quota figures come from Alberta (lucyk2017); Ontario hospitals used similar productivity standards, but no Ontario source was opened.

Loaded costs are the organisation file's ranges: hourly wage x 1.35 (about 25% benefits and HOOPP pension plus 10% overhead). Physician costs are gross clinical earnings paid by the province, not hospital payroll. Roles added here use the same 1.35 factor.
